column1: # The screens the documentation site shows, one row per screen.
# scripts/docs-capture.sh renders every row into <name>.ansi beside this file,
# under one pinned instant (2026-09-16T09:00:00Z — every fixture is a picture of
# that Wednesday), against the store scripts/demo-store.py builds. The files are
# committed; crates/tasqx-cli/src/fixtures.rs embeds them with include_str! and
# crates/tasqx-cli/src/ansi_html.rs renders them into the guide. CI re-captures
# and fails on a difference (DESIGN.md D149), so a screen that changed is a
# regenerated fixture in the same pull request.
# Columns, tab-separated. A line starting with # is a comment.
#   name    the fixture's file name, and the key fixtures::screen() takes
#   kind    pipe     read-only, rendered through a pipe
#           pipe-mut writes; runs against a COPY of the store, so rows cannot
#                    perturb each other or depend on the manifest's order
#           tui      full-screen; held in a tmux pane and captured with its SGR
#   cols    COLUMNS (pipe) or the pane's width (tui)
#   rows    the pane's height; - on a pipe row
#   args    the arguments after `tasqx --no-daemon`, quoted as a shell would
#   keys    keys sent before a tui row is captured, space-separated; - for none
#   stdin   the request envelope fed to `api`; - when nothing is piped in
# Two screens are deliberately absent, both because they cannot be reproduced on
# a second machine — which would make the drift job red for everyone but the
#   about                  prints the store's absolute path and the build's
#   api core.capabilities  its `store` is this machine's path too. The guide
#                          with a plausible store instead (D74, docs.rs's
#   api task.add           answers with a freshly minted v7 id, whose low bits
#                          are random; the pin fixes the timestamp half and
#                          nothing fixes the rest. The CLI's `add` echo
#                          (add-echo) shows the write instead, and prints a
#   any api response        carrying an FTS `rank` (`task.brief`, `memory.search`):
#                          bm25 is computed with the platform's `log()`, so the
#                          last digits differ between macOS and Linux. Captured
#                          on one, the drift job fails on the other — which is
#                          how this rule was found, on CI, with `api-task-brief`.
#                          The SCREENS over the same search are fine and stay
